geography_sector: UK/USA/Germany/Canada; HS2, California HSR, Berlin Brandenburg, Trans Mountain
definition: No PG definition. Governance trap = mismatch between law-mandated stakeholder inclusion and shareholder-centric investment decisions (p. 6).
elements: 2x2 framework (mandated stakeholder inclusion x shareholder-centric investment)
Unified Governance / Mandated Stakeholderism / Voluntary Stakeholderism / Institutionalized Inclusivity
stakeholders: Managers, stakeholders (communities/third parties), shareholders/investors; 'stakeholders can leverage their legal rights to delay projects' (p. 6); conflict = protracted bargaining, project stalls.
temporality_detail: Moderate & RQ-relevant. Planning-stage cost growth + political funding pulls; 'protracted bargaining cycles' (p. 7); regime contrast - HSR 'progressed rapidly in authoritarian regimes' while liberal democracies delay (p. 6). Not a cyclical electoral model.
megaproject_detail: HS2; California HSR; Berlin Brandenburg; Trans Mountain.
misalignment_detail: Adds a political-decision-reversal instance (Sunak cancels HS2 phase 2, 'The facts have changed,' p. 6) and a democracy-vs-authoritarian tempo contrast. Frames delay as stakeholder-bargaining, not electoral entrainment.
gaps: Governance-trap 2x2 is a ready mechanism to which the electoral clock can be added.
key_quotes: PM Sunak justified cancelling HS2 phase 2 by declaring, 'The facts have changed' (p. 6).
'stakeholders can leverage their legal rights to delay projects' (p. 6).
coding_notes: Reuses the shareholder/stakeholder axis from Joslin & Müller (2016). Strong megaproject + political-system framing.
